question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2y\,i+{x}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\sqrt{y}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(-1,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{t}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2t\,i+(\sqrt{t}-3)^{2}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}-3)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j) \\  & =2t\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =\sqrt{t}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =t-5\sqrt{t}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-5\sqrt{t}+9)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
